newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks dip below key levels as gloom spreads.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks dip below key levels as gloom spreads.

text.p: Tokyo stocks fell on Thursday as widening gloom about the health of the Japanese economy pushed the market's benchmark index below key psychological levels.
Tokyo's Nikkei average of 225 leading stocks slipped down under 20,000 points and then sank further through another closely watched level around 19,920 points where it had previously found a floor.
By mid-afternoon it was trading 156.92 points lower, or 0.78 percent down, at 19,936.11.

Brokers said a succession of poor performances by Tokyo stocks had compounded a feeling of gloom about the market and the overall Japanese economy, which is struggling to mount a full-blooded recovery from a long slump.
"Market sentiment was feeble to begin with as there are too many uncertainties surrounding the economy," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager.
"But after it fell below the technical support level this afternoon, market participants began to feel that the index should fall as far as it wants, until the only way left to go is up," he added.

Brokers added that the negativism was so strong that even relatively upbeat comments from the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor on Wednesday did little to mitigate the mood. The governor had said Japan's economic recovery was firming up.
"Investors are highly sceptical about Japan's economic health and they think that the BOJ is just trying to boost the sagging morale," one broker said.

On Wednesday, Japan's government issued a relatively modest forecast for economic growth in the next fiscal year but said the nation's recovery should continue. Continuing weakness in the economy would hold back corporate profits.

In recent weeks, the Tokyo stock market has been dragged down by a weaker Wall Street and general anxiety triggered by a warning from Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan about harmful "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.
After Greenspan's comments, the Nikkei posted its steepest plunge of the year, shedding 667.20 points by the end of the session on December 6.
Greenspan's remarks were seen as a warning that the United States might raise interest rates to put the brakes on the markets' ascent, which would have a knock-on effect on Japanese markets.

Tokyo stocks sank to their lowest close in nine months on Wednesday, ending down around 1.57 percent at 20,093.03. A rebound on Wall Street on Wednesday failed to inject much of a spark into the Japanese market.
